correctness.rationale: Taking complements in the ordinary cut definition gives precisely the complexes avoiding disconnected induced k-sets. I independently constructed KG(5,2), its line graph, both forbidden families and both full face posets; rebuilt the specified matching, and topologically sorted every reversed-cover diagram. For k=4,5 respectively: 1185/2556 forbidden sets, 767/2457 nonempty dual faces, 285/916 pairs with both recorded hashes reproduced, and 2355/9690 covers with every face processed. The complete critical-cell profiles are one point plus 196 two-cells and one point plus 624 three-cells, so Forman's CW theorem gives the integral wedges, with all higher cells attaching to the point. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality has shift 15-i-3=12-i and gives the asserted original homology in degrees 10 and 9. Direct enumeration of original cut-side faces and binary boundary ranks also agrees, but is not the integral proof.
residual_risks: Only k=4,5 for L(KG(5,2)); dual homotopy, not original cut-complex homotopy. The original-side computation checks only mod two.

value.rationale: The two neighboring ordinary cut thresholds on a natural symmetric line graph give exact integral test cases distinct from the Petersen graph and from the earlier grid settings. The full Morse certificate rules out hidden torsion and additional homotopy features on the duals despite the presence of higher-dimensional faces; either list of binary ranks alone would not do so. These provide concrete comparison cases for whether pure dual wedge behavior persists across thresholds in line graphs of cubic graphs.
residual_risks: A finite result on one host, not a line-graph family theorem.
